structured-output-contract-lab.name: Structured Output Contract Lab
structured-output-contract-lab.description: Turn model-formatted JSON into a versioned, validated, bounded application contract.
structured-output-contract-lab.hero: The model returned valid-looking JSON. Production still broke because syntax was never the real contract.
structured-output-contract-lab.quick: Structured output becomes reliable only when shape, semantics, repair behavior, and partial-state rules form one machine-verifiable boundary.
structured-output-contract-lab.transferPrompt: A downstream workflow adds a new required invariant. Which part of the contract must change without breaking older consumers?

brief.title: Valid JSON is not a valid business object.
brief.role: You own the boundary between an LLM extractor and an order workflow.
brief.body: An extraction endpoint parses successfully, but an empty items array violates a downstream invariant. Three blind retries increase latency without making the consumer safer.
brief.objective: Design a contract that rejects malformed and semantically invalid output before it crosses the application boundary.
brief.stakes: Weak contracts turn probabilistic output into deterministic downstream failures.

debrief.title: A contract is more than output shape.
debrief.rule: Parseability is evidence of syntax, not evidence of semantic validity.
debrief.body: Reliable structured output combines an explicit schema, domain validation, bounded repair, and clear streaming semantics. The model proposes data; the application owns the contract.
points: Version contracts instead of silently drifting them.
Validate domain invariants after structural validation.
Bound repair loops so failure cannot amplify indefinitely.

takeaways: JSON Schema cannot express every business invariant.
Retries need validation evidence and a stopping rule.
Partial output needs explicit consumer semantics.

next.title: Next: capability boundaries
next.description: Apply the same contract thinking to tools and MCP capabilities.

mcp-capability-boundary-mission.name: MCP Capability Boundary Mission
mcp-capability-boundary-mission.description: Design least-privilege MCP capability exposure against the current protocol model.
mcp-capability-boundary-mission.hero: Your Agent can read an order, refund it, update CRM, and export every customer. One broad identity exposes all of it.
mcp-capability-boundary-mission.quick: MCP capability discovery does not decide application authority; your runtime still owns authorization, least privilege, side-effect approval, and long-work boundaries.
mcp-capability-boundary-mission.transferPrompt: A server adds a new mutating capability tomorrow. Should your Agent inherit it automatically?

brief.title: Discovery is not permission.
brief.role: You own the Agent gateway in front of an MCP server.
brief.body: A customer-support Agent needs a small subset of capabilities, but a shared identity can invoke every exposed mutation. The current protocol is stateless request/response; long-running work belongs behind an explicit extension boundary rather than an implicit session.
brief.objective: Expose only the capabilities, identity scope, and approval path the workload actually needs.
brief.stakes: A planning error should not become an unrestricted external side effect.

debrief.title: Capability discovery and authorization are different layers.
debrief.rule: A server can announce a capability; only your application should decide whether this Agent may use it.
debrief.body: Current MCP architecture favors explicit capability discovery and stateless request/response. Secure Agent systems add scoped identity, least privilege, auditable side-effect policy, and an explicit boundary for long-running tasks.
points: Never treat discovered capability as inherited permission.
Use workload-scoped authority instead of one broad shared identity.
Put consequential side effects behind risk-appropriate controls.

takeaways: Protocol surface is not application policy.
Job lifecycle should not be smuggled into session assumptions.

next.title: Next: recovery
next.description: Now make an Agent survive process loss, replay, and cancellation.

long-running-agent-recovery-mission.name: Long-Running Agent Recovery Mission
long-running-agent-recovery-mission.description: Design durable state, idempotent replay, verified resume, and bounded cancellation for long-running Agents.
long-running-agent-recovery-mission.hero: The worker died at step 613. Restarting from zero repeats 147 external side effects.
long-running-agent-recovery-mission.quick: Long-running Agents need durable workflow state and replay semantics; process memory and prompt history are not a recovery architecture.
long-running-agent-recovery-mission.transferPrompt: A tool reports success, but your worker crashes before checkpointing it. What evidence can make resume safe?

brief.title: Resume without replaying the world.
brief.body: The process disappears after hundreds of completed actions. No durable checkpoint exists, cancellation is ignored, and external tools are not transactional.
brief.objective: Recover from worker loss without losing state, duplicating side effects, or letting obsolete jobs run forever.
brief.stakes: Long-running autonomy without recovery semantics converts routine infrastructure failure into silent data corruption and spend.

debrief.title: Durability is a workflow property, not a model capability.
debrief.rule: Resume is safe only when completed state and side effects can be independently reconstructed or verified.
debrief.body: A production Agent needs durable execution records, idempotent side-effect boundaries, a resume policy, and bounded cancellation. These guarantees live in the runtime around the model.
points: Persist enough state to reconstruct what actually completed.
Make replay safe at the same granularity you resume.
Cancellation must have a bounded operational meaning.

takeaways: Prompt history cannot replace workflow state.
Every resumed step needs a side-effect policy.

next.title: Apply the method to an outcome
next.description: Use the same source, context, verification, and workflow ideas to produce a book-length artifact.

write-book-with-ai-build.name: Write a Book with AI
write-book-with-ai-build.seoTitle: Write a Book with AI — AhaFrame Build
write-book-with-ai-build.description: Build a source-backed AI writing system for a coherent ten-chapter manuscript.
write-book-with-ai-build.hero: Ten fluent chapters are easy. A ten-chapter argument that stays sourced, coherent, and reviewable is the real build.
write-book-with-ai-build.quick: AI-assisted long-form writing is a knowledge workflow: source authority, argument structure, scoped context, claim verification, and editorial review must work together.
write-book-with-ai-build.transferPrompt: One authoritative source changes after six chapters are drafted. Which claims and chapter briefs must be invalidated?

brief.title: Design the manuscript system, not the magic prompt.
brief.role: You are producing an evidence-based ten-chapter book.
brief.body: Individual drafts read well, but terminology drifts, unsupported claims repeat, and only a fraction of claims trace back to sources.
brief.objective: Build a repeatable research-to-manuscript workflow with traceability and bounded revision cost.
brief.stakes: Publication quality depends on system-level consistency, not one-shot fluency.

debrief.title: Long-form creation is controlled context plus evidence.
debrief.rule: A larger context window does not replace source authority, argument dependencies, or factual verification.
debrief.body: The useful unit is a chapter brief linked to an argument map and a source base. Verification should review claims separately from prose quality, so revisions have clear provenance.
points: Separate research evidence from generated prose.
Give every chapter a job in the argument, not just a topic.
Invalidate dependent claims when authoritative sources change.

takeaways: Relevant chapter state beats manuscript dumping.
Fact checking is not copy editing.

next.title: Next: living knowledge
next.description: Turn the same source and retrieval principles into a maintained AI knowledge base.

knowledge-base-build.name: Build an AI Knowledge Base
knowledge-base-build.seoTitle: Build an AI Knowledge Base — AhaFrame Build
knowledge-base-build.description: Design an authority-aware, fresh, evaluated retrieval system instead of a document dump.
knowledge-base-build.hero: Your corpus contains the right policy—and two stale versions that rank higher.
knowledge-base-build.quick: A useful knowledge base is a lifecycle: ingestion, authority, retrieval, freshness, and evaluation must agree over time.
knowledge-base-build.transferPrompt: A frequently retrieved document is superseded. How do you prove the old policy stopped influencing answers?

brief.title: Make knowledge stay correct after launch.
brief.role: You own 4,800 product, policy, and support documents.
brief.body: Vector recall looks high, but source conflicts and stale policy copies produce wrong answers. Updates arrive days after the source of truth changes.
brief.objective: Design a retrieval lifecycle that favors authoritative evidence, refreshes quickly, and is regression-tested.
brief.stakes: Retrieval that works only in a demo becomes a stale-answer machine in production.

debrief.title: Knowledge is maintained, not merely embedded.
debrief.rule: Similarity is one retrieval signal; authority, freshness, exact identifiers, and evaluation determine whether evidence is usable.
debrief.body: A production knowledge base needs explicit source ownership, broad candidate recall, ranking policy, a fast update path, and a failure set that catches regressions.
points: Attach authority and ownership before retrieval starts.
Evaluate the retrieval pipeline with known failure classes.
Treat stale evidence as an operational incident, not a prompt problem.

takeaways: A dump lacks authority and lifecycle.
Ranking policy decides what evidence wins.
Updates need measurable latency and regression checks.

next.title: Next: support system
next.description: Use knowledge, tools, autonomy, and escalation together in a customer-support build.

customer-support-build.name: AI Customer Support Build
customer-support-build.description: Design a grounded, least-privilege support Agent with risk-based autonomy and escalation.
customer-support-build.hero: A support Agent found an outdated exception policy and issued a real refund.
customer-support-build.quick: Support automation is not one chatbot: knowledge authority, tool scope, autonomy boundaries, escalation, and auditability must compose into one operating system.
customer-support-build.transferPrompt: Which support intents can become fully autonomous, and which should always preserve a human approval boundary?

brief.title: Automate resolution without automating every risk.
brief.body: The Agent handles policy questions and account mutations with the same broad tool surface. Human escalation is model-decided, and an outdated policy already caused a wrong refund.
brief.objective: Increase resolution while making consequential actions bounded, grounded, auditable, and escalatable.
brief.stakes: A conversational mistake is recoverable; an incorrect account mutation may not be.

debrief.title: Autonomy should follow risk, not novelty.
debrief.rule: Ground answers in authority; scope tools by intent; require approval where side effects are consequential or ambiguous.
debrief.body: Strong support systems separate read-only assistance, low-risk automation, consequential mutations, and uncertain exceptions. Escalation is an explicit policy, not the model admitting that it feels unsure.
points: Use knowledge authority to ground policy decisions.
Expose the smallest tool surface that can complete the current intent.
Measure both automation quality and human queue load.

takeaways: Tool access changes the risk class.
Do not outsource the boundary to model self-confidence.

next.title: Next: knowledge products
next.description: Apply AI to curriculum and media production without turning the result into generated filler.

course-knowledge-product-build.name: Course / Knowledge Product Build
course-knowledge-product-build.seoTitle: Build a Course with AI — AhaFrame
course-knowledge-product-build.description: Design an AI-assisted course production system with objectives, concept reuse, editorial QA, media QA, and provenance.
course-knowledge-product-build.hero: Generating 42 lessons quickly is not success if they repeat facts, drift in voice, and teach no transferable capability.
course-knowledge-product-build.quick: AI knowledge-product production needs learning objectives, a reusable concept graph, editorial verification, media QA, and source provenance—not a queue of lesson prompts.
course-knowledge-product-build.transferPrompt: A new lesson re-explains a concept that already exists elsewhere. Should you duplicate the explanation or attach a new practice experience to the canonical concept?

brief.title: Scale production without scaling filler.
brief.role: You are producing a bilingual AI engineering course with media assets.
brief.body: Eighteen fast-generated drafts repeat concepts, prerequisites drift, editorial voice changes, and source provenance is incomplete.
brief.objective: Build a production system where AI accelerates drafting but learning design and publication quality stay inspectable.
brief.stakes: Content volume can rise while educational value falls.

debrief.title: AI can scale drafting faster than it scales judgment.
debrief.rule: Reuse canonical knowledge; generate practice around it; verify every artifact against explicit learning and publication criteria.
debrief.body: A scalable knowledge-product pipeline begins with measurable outcomes and concept identity, then uses AI to draft variants, examples, media, and exercises. Editorial and provenance gates decide what is publishable.
points: A topic list is not a learning objective.
Use one canonical concept across many paths instead of duplicating explanations.
Track provenance and media defects as publication constraints.

takeaways: One concept can serve many outcomes.
A second model pass is not independent QA.
Publication needs traceable sources and assets.

next.description: Connect these Builds back to the concepts and paths they practice.
